suppressed.reason: gunnery.ts is the combat balance table: 34 exports are named constants plus one-line pure functions over them. A wide flat surface is correct here — the alternative is the literals-in-game.ts arrangement the file was created to end. Judge: justified-by-domain.

player.ts exports PLAYER_FLIGHT and the flight-envelope constants precisely so no other module copies them. It is the fix for a one-rule-two-homes problem, not an instance of one. Judge: justified-by-domain.
scenario.ts exposes one Episode simulation facade plus the value types needed by trainers and viewers; its shared game-backed simulation sits behind that cohesive API. Judge: justified-by-domain.
navigation.ts gives each shared galaxy-distance and jump rule a named pure function so charts, gameplay, and headless campaign code cannot grow separate formulas. Judge: justified-by-domain.
hyperspace.ts is a pure decision/result boundary: its exported refusal and result types make jump checks exhaustive without exposing mutable implementation. Judge: justified-by-domain.
World is the explicit aggregate for scene objects and their lifetimes; its public fields and verbs are the owned world model, not unrelated forwarding exports. Judge: justified-by-domain.
rng.ts exports the complete seeded random-stream vocabulary so every simulation and headless harness uses one reproducible source instead of copied helpers. Judge: justified-by-domain.

Input is the platform boundary for frame-oriented keyboard and mouse state; the measured surface is one cohesive class API hiding DOM listener and tap-consumption machinery. Judge: justified-by-domain.
encounters.ts is a pure rule module whose constants, input/output types, timer factory, and step function form the complete testable encounter decision table. Judge: justified-by-domain.
systems.ts is the shared ship-durability and regeneration rulebook; named balance constants and pure transitions keep gameplay and survivability harnesses in parity. Judge: justified-by-domain.

views.ts is the intentionally tiny dependency-free home for cockpit orientations and their shared direction transform, extracted to remove a dependency cycle and duplicate formula. Judge: justified-by-domain.

ScreenHost hides overlay stack and routing rules behind the Screen contract; the apparent surface is mostly the finite ScreenId/ScreenOutcome protocol and cohesive host methods. Judge: justified-by-domain.
jettison.ts is a pure cargo-consequence rulebook whose thresholds, result types, and decisions let the game and campaign evaluate the same bribery and dumping rules. Judge: justified-by-domain.
DataScreen is one intentionally small Screen implementation; its context interface and class methods are the standard screen protocol, not mixed responsibilities. Judge: justified-by-domain.

combat-sim-scenarios.ts is an exported scenario and mode rules catalogue shared by the live trainer, reports, and tests; named data types and pure selectors are its intended product. Judge: justified-by-domain.

console.ts is intentionally the single six-line global boundary, with one publish and one read-back verb; merging it elsewhere would spread globalThis coupling into game code. Judge: justified-by-domain.
ContractsScreen is one cohesive Screen implementation; its context contract and lifecycle/input methods are the expected overlay boundary. Judge: justified-by-domain.

law.ts is the named legal-status and contraband balance table; exporting constants and pure classifications keeps UI, world rules, and campaign logic on the same definitions. Judge: justified-by-domain.
StatusScreen is a minimal Screen adapter from a narrow status context to rendering and input; its small size is the benefit of the common screen protocol. Judge: justified-by-domain.
Ordnance owns missile and energy-bomb transitions behind one class while exporting the event/reply value types and balance constants required by callers and tests. Judge: justified-by-domain.
slot.ts is the dependency-light single home for station-slot orientation, preventing the same three-line geometry rule being copied across world and docking modules. Judge: justified-by-domain.
population.ts is a pure population-planning table: exported probabilities, plan data, and planning functions let world creation and tests share one deterministic rule set. Judge: justified-by-domain.
BriefingScreen is one intentionally small implementation of the shared Screen protocol; its lifecycle methods hide its rendering and input details. Judge: justified-by-domain.

snapshot.ts exports a JSON schema and serialise/restore boundary; the public interfaces describe persisted data while conversion prevents classes and THREE objects leaking into saves. Judge: justified-by-domain.
trumbles.ts is a pure infestation rule set shared by gameplay and tests; its balance constants, event union, step, and message mapping are the domain API. Judge: justified-by-domain.
flight-controls.ts exposes two structural input value contracts and one pure FlightDemand producer so keyboard, replay, and tests share the same pilot rule. Judge: justified-by-domain.
missions.ts is a pure mission-state transition and presentation rulebook; its thresholds, event type, and focused queries are the complete shared domain vocabulary. Judge: justified-by-domain.
shop.ts is the canonical price and equipment catalogue; named prices, quote types, catalogue data, and ownership checks keep screens and campaign simulation consistent. Judge: justified-by-domain.
npc-targeting.ts contains one fleet-wide target-assignment pass plus its named range thresholds; hiding those constants would not deepen the single cohesive rule. Judge: justified-by-domain.
saves.ts groups the two save-related Screen implementations with the import/export/new-commander operations they orchestrate; the exports form one commander-file workflow. Judge: justified-by-domain.

commander.ts is the canonical plain-data model and pure commander rule set used by browser, storage, and headless campaign code; its types, limits, and queries are intentionally public. Judge: justified-by-domain.

combat-computer.ts hides policy observation and flight-demand generation behind CombatComputer; other exports are explicit state/value contracts and documented flight-envelope constants. Judge: justified-by-domain.

cargo.ts owns drifting cargo lifetimes behind CargoField and exports only the canister/reached contracts plus the shared scoop threshold needed at the consequence boundary. Judge: justified-by-domain.
The combat-sim-safety.ts back edge is `import type { ExerciseFit }` from combat-sim.ts; TypeScript erases it, so the reported cycle has no runtime dependency to break. Judge: justified-by-domain.
